### Python pipeline changes (no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.py)

_No changes._

### Plain-language summary

**Job 4774136's run again, with a different pipeline underneath it.** Every knob
is what job_4774136 used -- `union` scope, an empty lag set, all 468 channels --
so this is not a parameter experiment. It is the first real-data run of the code
written since, and the question it answers is whether the backbone gets deeper
when the two things that were starving it are removed.

**What changed in the code.** Two things, both aimed at the same symptom
(job_4774136 ended with 6 interior nodes and 23 external inputs):

1. **The depth cap is gone** (`NESTED_M` 1 -> 0 = uncapped). At `NESTED_M=1` the
   BFS expanded the targets and their drivers and then stopped, so anything one
   step further out was filed as an external input regardless of the evidence.
   Five of those 23 externals HAD drivers sitting in the precomputed table --
   `CA1_85_tsls` had six -- and the cap discarded them. The run precomputed 247
   MDE results and consulted 21. Uncapping is nearly free here because both
   scopes precompute the whole node universe up front; the budget only governs
   how much of that existing table the BFS reads. (The exception is `staged`
   WITH lags, where a larger visited set means more Stage 2 calls -- not this
   job.)

2. **The skill gates are now per metric**, looser for neurons. One 0.2 bar was
   applied to two metrics with different ceilings: `correlation` (the behavioural
   targets) can reach 1.0, while a near-perfect predictor of a real TSLS channel
   scores `f1` ~0.49-0.54 (`scripts/calibration/r9_min_pred_events_curve.csv`).
   So the shared bar demanded ~38% of achievable skill from a neuron and 20%
   from a behavioural target. The f1 gate is now 0.1 (= 0.20 x 0.52), about
   1.4 sigma above estimator noise at `MIN_PRED_EVENTS=20`. In job_4774136, 101
   nodes had no candidate clear the gate at all at 1-D; this is the direct
   attempt on that number.

Also in this run, though not aimed at the node count: Stage 2 is now skipped
outright when the lag set is empty (the `ZeroDivisionError` that killed
job_4774133), and generative fidelity / forecast rho are no longer reported for
real-data passthrough nodes, which were being cross-mapped against copies of
themselves and scoring 1.0. Those nodes are still drawn in the network figures;
only their scores are withheld.

**Why the tables above look so quiet.** `generate_job_description.sh` diffs the
sbatch file and the entry `.py`. Nearly all of the above lives in
`scripts/src/mde_gmn/`, which it does not diff, so "Python pipeline changes: no
changes" is true of the 45-line entry script and misleading about the run. The
`NESTED_M` row reads `${NESTED_M:-0}` for the same reason -- the generator sees
the file's text, not the resolved value; it resolved to 0, uncapped.

**Nothing is reused from the cache.** The per-node fingerprint hashes every
`*.py` in the package, so all four stages recompute from scratch. The resolved
gate (not the mapping) is in the fingerprint too, so a node computed under 0.2
can never be served to a run that asked for 0.1.

| Knob | Value | Via |
|---|---|---|
| `DELAY_SOURCE` | `explicit` | `--export` |
| `DELAY_SET` | `0` (-> EMPTY lag set) | `--export` |
| `REGION_CHANNEL_CAP` | `999` (all 468) | `--export` |
| `PARALLEL_MDE_SCOPE` | `union` | `--export` |
| `NESTED_M` | `0` = uncapped | file (new) |
| `EMBED_DIM_RHO_MIN` / `CROSS_MAP_RHO_MIN` | 0.2 | file, behavioural targets |
| `EMBED_DIM_RHO_MIN_F1` / `CROSS_MAP_RHO_MIN_F1` | 0.1 | file (new), neuronal nodes |
| `MDE_D` | 10 | file (half production) |
| `CCM_PREFILTER_RHO_MIN` | 0.2 | file default, deliberately left on |
| `CCM_SLOPE` | 0.01 | file; NOT split per type -- see below |

**What this job does not test.** `CCM_SLOPE` is still one threshold for both
target types. The slope harness
(`scripts/calibration/ccm_slope_distribution.py`) measured the distributions --
neuronal n=5,692, 15.7% at or above 0.01; behavioural n=163,927, 0.3% -- but the
logged slopes are only those of SELECTED candidates, censored at the current
threshold by construction, so no percentile of them can locate the right bar.
That needs a surrogate null, which has not been run.

**Read it against job_4774136.** Interior vs. external node counts, `realized
max depth`, and how many nodes still have no candidate clear the gate. If the
interior count does not move, the cause is not the depth cap or the f1 ceiling.

## Job 4774136

Generated: 2026-10-27T18:37:11+09:00

Git commit at submission: `1ae5883` (clean vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_4774133**

### Parameter changes (saion-no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch)

_No parameter changes._

### Batch script design changes (saion-no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch, excludes parameter block above)

_No changes._

### Python pipeline changes (no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.py)

_No changes._

### Plain-language summary

**The same Stage-1-only run under the other scope.** `PARALLEL_MDE_SCOPE=union`
with an empty lag set: one MDE per node over real and lagged candidates
together -- except there are no lagged candidates, so each node's pool is the
real observables alone, in a single pool with one barrier. Submitted as one of
a pair with job_4774133, which is the same thing under `staged`.

**What the pair is for.** Under lags the two scopes are genuinely different
algorithms, and `union`'s per-node pool is (1 + len(LAG_SET))x wider -- which
is what made job_4769437 unaffordable and ultimately OOM at 22h. With the lag
set empty that difference disappears: both should reduce to the same per-node
MDE over the same real-observable pool, with matching cache fingerprints. So
this job is also the empirical check of that equivalence against job_4774133.
Identical networks are the expected outcome; a difference would point at how
each scope enumerates the node universe, not at the selections themselves.

**Why the parameter table above says nothing changed.** All three knobs came
from the submitting shell, not the file: the sbatch is byte-identical to the
one job_4769464 ran, and `generate_job_description.sh` diffs the file. This
summary is the only record of what this job actually ran, so, in full:

| Knob | Value | Via |
|---|---|---|
| `DELAY_SOURCE` | `explicit` | `--export` |
| `DELAY_SET` | `0` | `--export` |
| `REGION_CHANNEL_CAP` | `999` | `--export` (made overridable in `1ae5883`) |
| `CCM_PREFILTER_RHO_MIN` | `0.2` | file default, deliberately left on |
| `PARALLEL_MDE_SCOPE` | `union` | `--export` |

**Zero lags.** `DELAY_SOURCE=explicit` with `DELAY_SET=0` resolves to an EMPTY
lag set -- `derive_lag_set()` strips every 0 entry on the explicit path. So
there are no lagged candidate columns, no Stage 2 picks, and no lagged leaf
nodes anywhere in the network.

**All channels, but still skill-gated.** `REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=999` offers all
468 real channels (CA1 147, OFC 234, mPFC 87) instead of 234. The CCM
pre-filter stays at `rho >= 0.2`, so it is now the only gate on the candidate
pool rather than the second of two. For reference, at CAP=78 it kept 127 of
234.

**Why.** job_4769178 (staged, lagged, 127 candidates) completed cleanly and
still produced an almost flat network: of its 98 edges exactly ONE driver was
a real observable (`CA1_53_tsls` -> both targets, delay 0, weight 0.42); all
97 others were lagged leaves, and the two targets' fidelity rho came out
negative (`head_position_x` -0.1253, `head_position_y` -0.0539) with every
start offset in the sweep scoring below zero. Two explanations fit that: the
real-observable pool was too thin (127 of 468 channels), or lagged candidates
outcompeted real ones inside each forward selection. Removing the lags and
widening the real pool separates the two -- whatever backbone this run finds
is built from real observables only.

**Cost.** Stage 2 is where essentially all of this pipeline's time goes, so
dropping it should bring the run down from job_4769178's 10h48m to hours:
job_4769464 (union, zero lags, 127 candidates) took 1h10m. The pool is ~3.7x
wider before the pre-filter, which widens each forward selection but adds no
(1 + len(LAG_SET))x lag expansion.

**Nothing is reused.** Both `lag_set` and `REGION_CHANNEL_CAP` are in the
per-node cache fingerprint, so this shares no cached node with any earlier
run and recomputes from scratch. The two jobs of this pair also run
CONCURRENTLY on saion-gpu11 (18+18 cores, 2+2 GPUs = exactly the per-partition
allocation), so the second cannot reuse the first's nodes either -- the cache
syncs hourly and is read from `/bucket` at startup. That duplicate compute is
accepted to get both answers in one wall-clock window.

**GPU sizing unchanged** (2 GPUs / 18 cores / 240 G). The OOM that stopped
job_4769437 at 22h is not expected here: per-call library size is set by
`MAX_WINDOW_ROWS`, not by how wide the candidate pool is, so a wider pool
means more calls rather than bigger ones -- and job_4769464, the zero-lag
union, logged zero CUDA errors.

Git commit at submission: `3cd63ab` (clean vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_4769350**

| Parameter | job_4769350 | job_4769437 |

### Batch script design changes (saion-no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch, excludes parameter block above)

_No changes._

### Python pipeline changes (no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.py)

_No changes._

### Plain-language summary

**`PARALLEL_MDE_SCOPE=union` at reduced CCM precision, 4 GPUs, hard 2-day
cap.** Supersedes job_4769350 (cancelled at 1h50m to free its 2 v100 GPUs;
it had logged 0 clamps, 0 OOMs and 0 failures, and had not yet reached the
`M=28251` call that killed job_4744295). Code is `3cd63ab`.

| | job_4744295 | job_4769350 | this job |
|---|---|---|---|
| partition | gpu-p100 | gpu-v100 | gpu-v100 |
| GPUs | 2 | 2 | **4** |
| cores | 18 | 4 | 18 |
| mem | 240 G | 80 G | 240 G |
| `CCM_SAMPLE` | 20 | 20 | **10** |
| `CCM_LIB_SIZES_ROWS` | 7 entries | 7 entries | **5** |
| time limit | 6 d | 6 d | **2 d** |

**4 GPUs is within allocation.** `sacctmgr` gives this account
`cpu=36,gres/gpu=4` on gpu-v100 and the same again, separately, on gpu-p100.
4 is therefore exactly the cap rather than an overrun -- but it needed
job_4769350's 2 GPUs back first, which is why that job was cancelled. Nothing
was lost: both knobs below are in the per-node cache fingerprint, so its
cached nodes would not have been reused anyway.

**Why these two knobs and not the five protected dimensions.** Every
observable (`REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=78`), driver (`MDE_D=10`), depth
(`NESTED_M=1`), the generative window (`GENERATE_LENGTH=400`), the lag set
(50 lags to -393) and all 44,449 data rows (`MAX_WINDOW_ROWS=30000`) are
untouched. `CCM_SAMPLE` and the library sweep cost CCM ESTIMATOR PRECISION
only: rho at each library size is now averaged over 10 random draws instead
of 20, and the convergence slope is fitted through 5 points instead of 7,
with the endpoints (16 and 800) kept because proper_ccm's verdict needs the
endpoint-to-endpoint change as well as the slope.

**Memory.** 18 cores over 4 GPUs is 5 workers/device, so the budget should
print ~14.5 GiB admissible (15.77 total, less 4 sibling contexts at 320 MiB
and the 1 GiB reserve). Halving `CCM_SAMPLE` also halves the GPU cross-map's
batch dimension, which is ~80% of a call by crossmap_bytes()'s terms, so the
worst union call should fall from the ~14.9 GiB it held in job_4744295 to
roughly 9 GiB -- a far wider margin than job_4769350's ~0.5 GiB. If that
estimate is wrong the run now stops and says so (`4bd0f9b`) rather than
recording unevaluated candidates as measured dead ends.

**It will NOT finish inside the 2 days.** job_4744295's final heartbeat
projected ~34 more days at 18 cores / 2 GPUs / 20 samples / 7 library sizes.
Doubling the GPUs (~2x), halving the batch (~1.7x) and dropping to 5 library
sizes (~1.4x) is about 4.7x altogether, i.e. roughly 7 days of work. The
2-day limit is an OCCUPANCY cap, deliberately, not a completion estimate:
USR1 fires at 1d23h30m for a clean stage-out, the per-node cache is synced to
Bucket hourly, and resubmitting resumes from every finished node. Expect
around four 2-day windows, with the cluster released between each.

**No cache head start, and not comparable to job_4769178.** `ccm_sample` and
`ccm_lib_sizes_rows` are both inside `build_mde_selection_fingerprint` /
`build_multi_mde_selection_fingerprint`, so this run correctly MISSES every
node cached at the old precision instead of silently reusing it -- it begins
from scratch. By the same token it cannot be compared against job_4769178,
which is mid-flight at `CCM_SAMPLE=20` and 7 library sizes. A valid
staged-vs-union pair needs both sides at the same precision.

## Job 4769350

Generated: 2026-10-22T17:29:03+09:00

Git commit at submission: `2f8da11` (clean vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_4769178**

### Parameter changes (saion-no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch)

_No parameter changes._

### Batch script design changes (saion-no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch, excludes parameter block above)

_No changes._

### Python pipeline changes (no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.py)

_No changes._

### Plain-language summary

**`PARALLEL_MDE_SCOPE=union`, the partner to job_4769178's `staged`, on the
same fixed code (`2f8da11`).** Every science parameter is identical to
job_4744295 -- the union run that died -- including `MAX_WINDOW_ROWS=30000`
and `CCM_SAMPLE=20`. Only the resource request changed, and only to make
the memory arithmetic work:

| | job_4744295 (OOM'd) | this job |
|---|---|---|
| partition | gpu-p100 | **gpu-v100** |
| GPUs | 2 | 2 |
| cores | 18 | **4** |
| mem | 240 G | **80 G** |
| workers/device | 9 | **2** |

**Why 4 cores and not 18.** The binding constraint is not total GPU memory,
it is the per-worker CUDA context: ~320 MiB that every worker holds from
start to exit whether or not it is computing, which is why create_budgets()
subtracts it per worker sharing the card. The worst call in job_4744295 --
`proper_ccm CA1_48_tsls::delay-41->CA1_43_tsls M=28251 B=20` -- actually
needed about **14.9 GiB**: at the moment it OOM'd it held 13.22 GiB and was
asking for 1.69 GiB more. At 9 workers/device the sibling contexts cost
9 x 320 MiB = 2.81 GiB, leaving only ~13.1 GiB physically reachable by a
clamped request, roughly **1.8 GiB short** -- which is exactly why it
failed. At 2 workers/device the sibling cost falls to ~0.31 GiB, leaving
~15.46 GiB against ~14.9 GiB needed: a margin of about **0.56 GiB**.

Note that `crossmap_bytes()` ESTIMATED that same call at 50.66 GiB, ~3.4x
its observed actual. So admission control will clamp the big calls and hand
the device over rather than admitting them against the budget -- that is the
intended path here, and it is what lets them fit at all. (The estimate's
true headroom factor is still unmeasured; see `2f8da11` on why the old
UNDER-ESTIMATED figures were measurement artefact.)

**Why gpu-v100 rather than the rest of gpu-p100.** The 36-core/4-GPU
allocation is attached to each partition SEPARATELY, so running here costs
job_4769178 nothing and the two never queue against each other. It uses
4 of 36 cores and 2 of 4 GPUs of the gpu-v100 entitlement, leaving 2 GPUs
and 32 cores of saion-gpu22 free for other people. V100 is 15.77 GiB
against P100's 15.89, i.e. marginally SMALLER -- the partition choice is
about contention, not capacity; no card available on this account (there is
no gpu-a100 allocation) is larger than ~16 GiB.

**This does not make OOM impossible, and on 16 GiB cards nothing can.**
The margin on the single worst call is ~0.5 GiB. What has changed is the
consequence: if it is exceeded the run now STOPS (`4bd0f9b`, `2f8da11`)
instead of recording 20 unevaluated candidates as measured dead ends the
way job_4744295 did, the hourly-synced cache keeps every finished node, and
the log names the call and its shape so the next decision rests on a
measurement rather than a guess.

**What was deliberately NOT changed.** Lowering `MAX_WINDOW_ROWS` is the
other way to make the big calls fit, and it was rejected: job_4769178 is
running `staged` at 30000 right now, and the entire purpose of a scope pair
is to compare staged against union. Shrinking one side's library window
would leave the two incomparable, which costs more than it buys.

**Expect it to be slow.** 4 workers against job_4744295's 18, on a scope
that had not completed in 39 h. It will very likely reach the 6-day wall;
resubmitting continues from the cache rather than restarting.

### Python pipeline changes (no-kedm-optimization-parallelized-mde--tsls-mde-gmn.py)

_No changes._

### Plain-language summary

**The first run of the fixed pipeline.** Same scope and parameters as
job_4744294 (`PARALLEL_MDE_SCOPE=staged`, `LAG_STEP=8`,
`REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=78`, `GENERATE_LENGTH=400`, 2 GPUs / 18 cores /
240 G). Nothing about the science or the sizing changed; what changed is
three bugs, none of which the diffs above can show, because
generate_job_description.sh only diffs the sbatch and the ENTRY script
and every fix landed in `mde_gmn/` or `gpu_budget.py`. Commits
`ecbba37`, `4bd0f9b`, `2f8da11`.

**1. Why job_4744294 lost a network (`ecbba37`).** It ran 19h, exited 0,
and produced no plots, fidelity or output for
`head_position_x_head_position_y`. `_generalized_embed` looked up a
`(col, delay)` coordinate under the RAW observable name first and the
pre-shifted `<obs>::delay<n>` name only as a fallback. During a
`Generate()` run a node's frame carries every column in the network but
populates only the coordinates that node owns, so a raw name can be
present and still hold nothing: `OFC_10_tsls`'s coordinate
`(CA1_55_tsls, -305)` found a raw column with 1 valid row of 37783,
shifted it to all-NaN, and ignored the pre-shifted column beside it
holding 37478 real values. pyEDM then dropped every row carrying a NaN
-- all 37478 -- which emptied the library, made SMap's
`knn = len(lib_i) - 1 = -1`, and reached scipy as a reduction over an
empty array: `zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has
no identity`, 22 times. Pre-shifted now wins for any nonzero delay;
delay 0 still reads the raw (growing, simulated) column, which it must.
This completes `551b59b`, which added the pre-shifted branch but left
raw-first priority. Verified by replaying the exact `Generate()` that
died: it now completes 400 rows with 0 NaN.

**2. Why that was silent, and is not any more (`ecbba37`, `2f8da11`).**
`_generalized_embed` now refuses an all-NaN coordinate and names it,
instead of letting it surface unrecognisably hundreds of frames later.
And STATUS.txt now counts `NETWORKS_SKIPPED` and FAILs on it: a network
that rebuilds nothing previously reached STATUS.txt nowhere at all,
which is how job_4744294 reported `pipeline exited 0` while having lost
a target pair.

**3. Why job_4744294's FAIL reason was wrong (`2f8da11`).** It read
"93 CUDA error line(s)". All 93 were `GPU budget: UNDER-ESTIMATED`
advisories, printed AFTER a reservation is granted and the call has run;
there were ZERO real CUDA errors in the whole run. `UNDER-ESTIMATED` is
out of the CUDA-error pattern and now reports on its own line as
`GPU_BUDGET_ADVISORIES`. The advisory itself was also untrustworthy: it
compared the estimate against `max_memory_reserved()`, a process-wide
high-water mark, so a small call inherited whatever a larger one had
cached before it in the same worker -- hence job_4744295's 73x readings
on `M=1003` calls whose own tensors come to ~0.1 GiB. It measures growth
over a baseline now. `crossmap_bytes()`'s headroom factor is
deliberately UNCHANGED: the old figures were partly measurement
artefact, so the true factor is still unmeasured and a union run is the
first thing that can report it honestly.

**4. GPU memory failures can no longer become findings (`4bd0f9b`,
`2f8da11`).** A candidate dropped for want of memory is a missing edge,
and downstream it is indistinguishable from one measured and found
absent -- so swallowing it fabricates a negative result. `gpu_budget`
re-raises for exactly that reason and says so in its error text, but
every caller answering a failed MDE call with `_failed_mde_result()`
caught `Exception` broadly and wrote a dead end anyway: job_4744295
printed "the run is stopping rather than recording it as a dead end" 20
times and then recorded 20 dead ends. All six such sites now ask
`mde.is_gpu_memory_failure()` first and stop the run. Genuine findings
(short data, no CCM convergence) still fall through to the dead-end path.

**What to expect.** This is `staged`, which had zero genuine OOMs in
job_4744294, so change 4 should not trigger; it matters for `union`.
The run reaches the `Generate()` stage that failed last time at roughly
the 19h mark, and that is the checkpoint worth watching. Resubmitting
after a timeout is cheap -- every finished MDE node is cached and synced
hourly. NOT submitted as a scope pair: `union` is left until its worker
count comes down, because at 9 workers/device the per-request ceiling is
12.1 GiB (15.9 total, less 9 x 320 MiB of resident sibling CUDA contexts
and a 1 G safety reserve) and job_4744295 asked for 13.22 GiB, so it
would now stop at the first genuine OOM rather than quietly losing
candidates.

real headroom, rather than waiting to see if job_40582445 finishes or
times out first. The `--cpus-per-task` bump (16->64) also directly
targets Stage 2's own per-node inner-parallelism: this wave has 7 nodes

should meaningfully speed up each node's own ranking-stage/CCM-gate work,
not just add idle headroom.

### Result

**Success.** `PIPELINE COMPLETE -- 9467.4s total` (~2.6h). **R22 fix
confirmed on a real run**, not just the toy regression test: the
`gmn_generate_forecast_head_position_x_head_position_y` figure now shows
the Forecast() trace correctly windowed around `generate_start` (~row
38070) with no stray mislabeled trace near time 0, and `FORECAST_PLOT_RANGE=
windowed` now actually clips the view as intended.

Same depth-0 outcome as job 40421505: `GMN_MODE=combined`'s joint gate
selected zero real observables again, so the entire 11-node network came
from Stage 2's own lagged-driver search.

**Generate() fidelity**: `head_position_y` correlation 0.915 (strong,
close to job 40421505's own 0.960); `head_position_x` -0.369 (poor,
anti-correlated -- consistent with job 40421505's -0.363). Driver-node f1
fidelity: 9/9 drivers score 1.0 for the Generate()-based per-node score.

**Forecast() rho (now meaningful, post-R22)**: `head_position_y` -0.509,
`head_position_x` 0.350 -- both weak/poor one-step-ahead skill for the
two targets themselves, while all 9 driver (non-target) nodes score a
perfect 1.0 f1. Separately, `gmn_fidelity_rho()` (a different, harder
test -- does a fresh Simplex predict the real series *from* the
generated series) is much more mixed for those same drivers: `CA1_10_tsls`
1.0, `CA1_14_tsls` 0.976, `OFC_5_tsls` 0.857, but `CA1_2_tsls`, `mPFC_5_tsls`,
`mPFC_9_tsls`, `mPFC_4_tsls`, `OFC_1_tsls`, `OFC_7_tsls` all score 0.0 --
several drivers predict one step ahead well but their own free-running
Generate() trajectory doesn't reproduce the real dynamics closely enough
for this stricter cross-check.

`RUN_MDE_EVALUATE=false` skipped cleanly; both targets' Tp-vs-rho sweep
skipped as designed (zero MDE-selected columns each, since the joint
depth-0 seed found nothing).

### Plain-language summary

Same scale/config as job 40421505 (REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=15, MDE_D=4,
NESTED_M=3, LAG_STEP=4, GMN_MODE=combined, TP=20,
FORECAST_PLOT_RANGE=windowed) -- no parameter changes. This run re-exercises
that same configuration purely to pick up code changes made since:

- **R22 fix (the diff shown above)**: `gmn_generate_forecast_*_part*.png`
  from job 40421505 showed every subplot with a small, mislabeled
  `Forecast()` trace stuck near the very start of the recording (x≈0), a
  huge gap, then the real `generate_start`-anchored cluster -- and
  `FORECAST_PLOT_RANGE="windowed"` looked identical to `"full"` because of
  it. Root cause (docs/review-findings.md's R22, traced through `gmn`'s own
  source, not guessed): the `EXTERNAL_INPUT_MODE='real_data'` leaf
  passthrough in `_generalized_node_forecast()` returned the network's
  *entire* dataset instead of a `pred`-range slice: since `gmn.GMN.Forecast()`
  takes its shared `Time` column only from whichever node is first in
  topological order (almost always a leaf, since leaves have no in-edges),
  that full-length passthrough silently defined `DataOut`'s own row index --
  every other node's own short, correctly-computed prediction window then
  pandas-aligned onto the *first* few hundred of those labels, relabeling
  data genuinely computed near `generate_start` as though it occurred at
  time 0. This wasn't just a plotting quirk: the `Forecast f1`/
  `Forecast correlation` scores printed in each subplot's own title were
  being scored against real data from the start of the recording instead of
  the actual `generate_start` window, so every such score from job 40421505
  onward (until this fix) should be treated as invalid. Fixed by slicing the
  leaf passthrough to the same `pred` range every other node already uses,
  plus an explicit `ax.set_xlim(plot_start, plot_end)` added as a defensive
  second layer. Regression-tested against a real (tiny) `gmn.GMN(...).Forecast()`
  call, not just inspected in isolation (`tests/test_r22_forecast_window_alignment.py`
  -- confirmed to genuinely fail without the fix and pass with it, by
  temporarily reverting and re-testing). Does **not** affect `Generate()`'s
  own outputs/fidelity scoring (`gmn_fidelity_rho()`) -- that path already
  used each node's own correctly-computed window, independent of this bug.
- **Interactive 3D network plot redesign** (`network_3d_{network_id}.png`
  -> `.html`): `plot_3d_network()` now renders via `plotly` instead of a
  static matplotlib PNG. Only nodes nested-MDE actually found drivers for
  (Stage 1/2 network members) sit on the x-y plane; every driver with no
  drivers of its own (a real-observable leaf, or a lagged copy of an
  observable -- including a node's own AR self-loop) is lifted onto the
  z-axis as its own distinct point, with arrows (fanning out to every node
  it actually feeds, rather than duplicated once per consumer as the old
  design did) showing the real driver relationships, rotatable/zoomable/
  hoverable in a browser. `simple-mde-gmn.py`'s own copy of this function is
  deliberately left as the old static PNG for now (not ported).
- **`multi_proper_mde` per-candidate auto-embedding-dimension** (already
  active in this config via `GMN_MODE=combined`): `MULTI_MDE_E` is now a
  ceiling (ceiling=3 here) for a per-candidate auto-selected E, via the new
  `multi_proper_embed_dimension()`, rather than one static E applied
  identically to every candidate in the joint CCM gate -- confirmed against
  a brute-force independent recomputation that different candidates
  genuinely resolve to different E values.

None of this changes network topology or Generate() fidelity -- expect this
run's own selected drivers/generated trajectories to look similar to job
40421505's, with a correct (not mislabeled) Forecast() diagnostic figure and
scores, and the new interactive HTML network figure in place of the old PNG.

### Plain-language summary

Same mid-scale calibration config as job 40386309, but with `LAG_STEP`
dropped from 1 to 4 (`GMN_MODE=combined`, `TP=20`, `GENERATE_LENGTH=200`,
`NESTED_M=3` also carried over from the hand-tuning between those two
jobs) -- submitted specifically to test whether a coarser Stage 2 lag
stride fixes the runaway Stage 2 cost diagnosed on job 40386309 (a single
node's forward-selection loop consuming 100+ dimensions to select many
different delays of only a handful of distinct real observables, each
dimension re-ranking almost the entire candidate pool -- confirmed via a
live `py-spy` stack dump; see `docs/review-findings.md`).

**Result: success, and the fix is confirmed.** `PIPELINE COMPLETE --
10443.9s total` (~2.9h) -- the first mid-scale (`REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=15`)
run to reach a clean finish. Direct before/after against job 40386309's
own per-node Stage 2 timings: `head_position_y` 25731.3s -> 2645.9s
(~9.7x), a zero-selection node 26536.2s -> 35.4s (~750x), whole Stage 2
wave 26536.4s -> 2681.4s (~9.9x). `RUN_MDE_EVALUATE=false` skipped
cleanly as designed.

**Real (mixed) fidelity results, reported honestly:** `head_position_y`
Generate() fidelity correlation 0.960 (strong); `head_position_x`
-0.363 (poor -- actually anti-correlated with the real trajectory).
Driver-node f1 fidelity: 7/9 drivers score 1.0; `CA1_2_tsls` and
`mPFC_4_tsls` both score 0.0. Both targets' depth-0 joint seed
(`multi_proper_mde` under `GMN_MODE=combined`) found zero real
observables directly -- the entire 11-node, 62-edge network came from
Stage 2's own lagged-pool search instead, which always runs on every
node regardless of Stage 1's own outcome there.

### Plain-language summary

The first mid-scale run of this pipeline since the metric-routing,
window-sizing, progress-monitoring, and R19 toggle/guard/timeout changes
all landed (committed as `3d925f9`/`d0a5b1b` just before this
submission). Steps up from job 40385630's smoke-test config
(`REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=3`/`MDE_D=2`/`NESTED_M=2`/`GENERATE_LENGTH=40`,
confirmed reaching `"Pipeline complete"` in 1089.8s) to
`REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=15`/`MDE_D=4`/`NESTED_M=1`/`GENERATE_LENGTH=100` --
deliberately reproducing job 38976891's own historical configuration,
which timed out after 4+ hours on a single depth-1 wave under the old
(fixed-800-row-window, metric-routing-bug-affected) code.

Resources also stepped up (`--time=2:00:00`→`24:00:00`,
`--mem=16G`→`32G`, `--cpus-per-task=8`→`16`) -- reasoned, not copied from
the old 4-day/128G/64-core VALIDATION tier: 24h is 6x job 38976891's own
budget that this identical configuration already exhausted once, sized
generously because the window-sizing redesign is a genuine
cost-increasing change at this scale (a slow-firing neuron can now
resolve a ranking window up to 30,000 rows, vs. the old fixed 800) that
has never been measured here, not because this run is expected to be
slow. `RUN_MDE_EVALUATE` stays `false` -- the diffusion-map hang is still
undiagnosed, and this is the wrong run to first exercise it at scale.

**What this run is actually for:** both a real calibration-scale data
point for the pipeline's own "isolate Stage 1's real cost driver at
REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=15" open question (docs/tsls-mde-gmn-pipeline.pdf,
Future Directions), and the next concrete step the same document's own
Capabilities section calls for. A timeout here is itself a useful,
informative result, not a sizing failure -- see the sbatch script's own
extended resource-reasoning comment for the full argument.

## Job 40385403

Generated: 2026-08-30T23:02:54+09:00

Git commit at submission: `93e7f3e` (uncommitted local changes vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_40143104**

### Plain-language summary

**Purpose: confirm the smoke configuration reaches "Pipeline complete" with
`RUN_MDE_EVALUATE=false`**, after job_40143104 crashed inside R19's
diffusion-map baseline (`run_mde_evaluate()`'s PCA/diffusion-map comparison)
and a follow-up isolated reproduction found that same baseline can also hang
indefinitely (74+ CPU-minutes, no completion, at real ~31,000-row scale) --
see `docs/review-findings.md`'s "Diffusion-map crash and hang in
`run_mde_evaluate()`" section for the full investigation.

**What's new since job_40143104** (uncommitted, not yet on a named branch):
a new `RUN_MDE_EVALUATE` toggle (default `false`, exposed in both sbatch
scripts, wired into `tsls-mde-gmn.py` only) gates R19's own diagnostic
separately from `RUN_MDE_DIAGNOSTICS` -- R7's own two diagnostics
(`run_tp_vs_rho_sweep`/`run_univariate_e_tau_grid`) are unaffected and still
run. `run_mde_evaluate()` itself now runs its PCA/diffusion-map baselines in
a genuinely separate process each, killed if either exceeds a 300s wall-clock
bound (`MDE_EVALUATE_BASELINE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) -- a subprocess-based bound
rather than a signal-based "soft" timeout, since the hang can occur inside
compiled KD-tree/BLAS calls that don't yield control back to Python's
interpreter for a signal handler to run. With the toggle off, none of this
new machinery is exercised this run -- R19 is skipped and logged once,
`main()` should reach every stage after it (R7, "Pipeline complete") for the
first time at this smoke scale.

### Parameter changes (tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch)

| Parameter | job_40143104 | job_40385403 |
|---|---|---|
| RUN_MDE_EVALUATE | _(unset)_ | false |

### Batch script design changes (tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch, excludes parameter block above)

```diff
+export TSLS_MDE_GMN_RUN_MDE_EVALUATE="${RUN_MDE_EVALUATE}"

 export TSLS_MDE_GMN_TARGET_METRIC="${TARGET_METRIC}"
```

```diff
+def _score_baseline(target_pred, predicted, targets, combined, target_metric, gamma_delta):
+    '''Shared scoring step for run_mde_evaluate()'s PCA/diffusion-map
+    baselines -- factored out so both baselines' own try/except blocks
+    (see that function's own docstring on why they're independently
+    guarded) call one identical implementation rather than two copies of

+            for i in range(len(targets))

+
+# Wall-clock bound for run_mde_evaluate()'s own PCA/diffusion-map baselines
+# (docs/review-findings.md's "diffusion-map crash and hang" finding): a
+# real diffusion-map fit on real TSLS data, at real (~31,000-row) scale,
+# has been observed to run past 74 CPU-minutes with no completion, crash,
+# or any output at all -- a non-raising hang a try/except cannot catch,
+# since there's nothing to except until the call returns control. Not
+# calibrated against a known-good completion time (no successful fit at
+# this scale has yet been observed to time); chosen as generous headroom
+# over the 1.8s a genuine crash takes to surface, while still bounding the
+# worst case to a tolerable, one-time-per-network cost.
+MDE_EVALUATE_BASELINE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300
+
+
+def _pca_baseline_worker(queue, pool_lib, pool_pred, target_lib, D):
+    '''Runs in a genuinely separate process -- see
+    _run_baseline_with_timeout()'s own docstring for why. Catches its own
+    exception and puts it on the queue rather than letting the child
+    process's own traceback (still visible in the job's .err) be the only
+    record -- so the parent can log it in run_mde_evaluate()'s own
+    existing "FAILED for {targets}: {exc!r}" style regardless of which
+    process actually raised it.'''
+    try:
+        pca = PCA(n_components=D)
+        pca.fit(pool_lib)
+        pca_lib_proj, pca_pred_proj = pca.transform(pool_lib), pca.transform(pool_pred)
+        pca_predicted = LinearRegression().fit(pca_lib_proj, target_lib).predict(pca_pred_proj)
+        queue.put(('ok', pca_predicted, pca_pred_proj))
+    except Exception as exc:
+        queue.put(('error', repr(exc), None))
+
+
+def _dmap_baseline_worker(queue, pool_lib, pool_pred, target_lib, D, dmap_k, dmap_epsilon):
+    '''Same contract as _pca_baseline_worker() above.'''
+    try:
+        dmap_model = dmap.DiffusionMap.from_sklearn(
+            n_evecs=D, k=dmap_k, epsilon=dmap_epsilon,
+            neighbor_params={'n_jobs': -1, 'algorithm': 'kd_tree'},
+        )
+        dmap_model.fit(pool_lib)
+        dmap_lib_proj, dmap_pred_proj = dmap_model.transform(pool_lib), dmap_model.transform(pool_pred)
+        dmap_predicted = LinearRegression().fit(dmap_lib_proj, target_lib).predict(dmap_pred_proj)
+        queue.put(('ok', dmap_predicted, dmap_pred_proj))
+    except Exception as exc:
+        queue.put(('error', repr(exc), None))
+
+
+def _run_baseline_with_timeout(worker_fn, args, timeout_seconds=MDE_EVALUATE_BASELINE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):
+    '''Runs worker_fn(queue, *args) in a genuinely separate process,
+    force-killed if it exceeds timeout_seconds -- the wall-clock bound
+    run_mde_evaluate()'s own PCA/diffusion-map guards need underneath
+    their existing exception handling (docs/review-findings.md's
+    "diffusion-map crash and hang" finding: a try/except plus a
+    signal-based "soft" timeout is not enough here, since pydiffmap's own
+    KD-tree/BLAS calls can run for a long time without ever returning
+    control to the Python interpreter -- a signal fires but its handler
+    can't actually run until the call returns on its own, which is
+    exactly the case that needs covering. Only an OS-level SIGKILL of a
+    genuinely separate process reclaims control regardless of what the
+    computation is doing internally). Cost: one process fork per baseline
+    call (cheap under `fork` -- no re-import, copy-on-write memory, real
+    overhead is milliseconds) plus pickling the (modest-sized, D-column)
+    result back through a Queue; the real cost is that a hard kill on
+    timeout discards whatever progress a slow-but-would-eventually-
+    succeed computation had made, converting it into a skip -- the
+    deliberate trade for a bounded worst case instead of an unbounded one.
+
+    Returns (status, value): ('ok', predicted_and_proj_tuple) on success;
+    ('timeout', None) if force-killed; ('error', repr(exc)) if the worker
+    itself raised (only ever read in the success path below -- the
+    process has already finished and flushed its queue write by the time
+    proc.join() returns non-alive, so there is no kill-mid-write race to
+    guard against).'''
+    ctx = mp.get_context('fork')
+    queue = ctx.Queue()
+    proc = ctx.Process(target=worker_fn, args=(queue, *args))
+    proc.start()
+    proc.join(timeout_seconds)
+    if proc.is_alive():
+        proc.terminate()
+        proc.join(5)
+        if proc.is_alive():
+            proc.kill()
+            proc.join()
+        return 'timeout', None
+    try:
+        status, a, b = queue.get_nowait()
+    except Exception:
+        return 'error', f'child process exited without a result (exitcode={proc.exitcode})'
+    if status == 'ok':
+        return 'ok', (a, b)
+    return 'error', a
+
```

## Job 40143104

Generated: 2026-08-28T22:42:53+09:00

Git commit at submission: `93e7f3e` (clean vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_40143067**

### Plain-language summary

**Purpose: exercise the new progress-monitoring log on a real cluster run,
at the user's explicit request**, after job_40143067 (still running,
started before this feature landed and so left untouched) confirmed the
`/bucket` outage from earlier tonight has cleared. Same
`REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=3/MDE_D=2/NESTED_M=2` smoke config as job_40143067 --
no parameter changes, per the table below.

**What's new since job_40143067** (see `docs/review-findings.md` for the
full design): `cfg['RESULTS_DIR']/progress.log`, written continuously by
the orchestrating process only. Stage 1/Stage 2 BFS -- this pipeline's own
confirmed historical bottleneck -- get per-node start/end lines with
duration, a heartbeat every 5 minutes while a wave is still running so a
long wave no longer goes silent the way job 38976891's own 4+ hour stall
did, and an ETA weighted by each pending node's own speculatively-resolved
window size. Every other step (depth-0 seed, GMN construction, theta
retuning, generate-start sweep, Generate/Forecast rebuild, R7/R19
diagnostics) gets simple start/end/duration logging. The sbatch script's
own `cleanup()` trap now appends a final `JOB ENDED: PY_STATUS=...
SLURM_STATE=...` line to the same log via `sacct`, so a crash/timeout/OOM
leaves an explicit record instead of the file just going silent.

**What to check in this job's own `progress.log`** (readable on `/flash`
while the job is still running, at
`/flash/FukaiU/j-tominaga/pao_rotation_results/job_40143104/progress.log`
once `$OUT_DIR` is created): a `PIPELINE START` line near the top, per-node
`stage1`/`stage2` START/END lines with real durations as Stage 1/2 run,
at least one `HEARTBEAT` line if any wave takes longer than 5 minutes, and
eventually a `JOB ENDED` line from the sbatch trap once the job finishes
one way or another.

_No parameter changes._

### Batch script design changes (tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch, excludes parameter block above)

```diff
--- job_40143067/tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch
+++ job_40143104/tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch
@@ -126,7 +126,33 @@
 # archive. Same mechanism as simple-mde-gmn.sbatch's own `cleanup` trap.
 SLURM_OUT="$FLASH_BASE/pao_rotation_results/${SLURM_JOB_NAME}-${SLURM_JOB_ID}.out"
 SLURM_ERR="$FLASH_BASE/pao_rotation_results/${SLURM_JOB_NAME}-${SLURM_JOB_ID}.err"
+# How the job actually ended, appended to the progress-monitoring log
+# (RESULTS_DIR/progress.log -- see tsls-mde-gmn.py's own _log_progress()
+# docstring) so a crash/timeout/OOM has an explicit, unambiguous final
+# line instead of the file just going silent. This is the one piece of
+# that log that CANNOT be written by Python itself: a hard kill means the
+# Python process never gets to write anything of its own. `$?` alone
+# (PY_STATUS below) can't distinguish OOM from a plain crash from a
+# timeout, so this queries sacct -- SLURM's own authoritative record --
+# with a couple of retries since its accounting can lag a few seconds
+# right at job-end. Honest limitation, not hidden: a true instantaneous
+# whole-cgroup SIGKILL (rare) can prevent this trap itself from running --
+# `sacct -j <job_id>` run separately, after the fact, is the authoritative
+# fallback in that case regardless of what this managed to write.
+log_final_outcome() {
+    local progress_log="$OUT_DIR/progress.log"
+    [ -f "$progress_log" ] || return 0
+    local slurm_state=""
+    for _ in 1 2 3; do
+        slurm_state="$(sacct -j "$SLURM_JOB_ID" --format=State -P -n 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d ' ')"
+        [ -n "$slurm_state" ] && break
+        sleep 2
+    done
+    echo "$(date -Iseconds) JOB ENDED: PY_STATUS=${PY_STATUS:-unset} SLURM_STATE=${slurm_state:-unknown (sacct had no record yet -- check \`sacct -j $SLURM_JOB_ID\` manually)}" \
+        >> "$progress_log"
+}
 cleanup() {
+    log_final_outcome
     [ -f "$SLURM_OUT" ] && mv -f "$SLURM_OUT" "$OUT_DIR"/
     [ -f "$SLURM_ERR" ] && mv -f "$SLURM_ERR" "$OUT_DIR"/
     if [ "${PY_STATUS:-1}" = "0" ] && [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ]; then
```

## Job 40142455

Generated: 2026-08-28T21:50:57+09:00

Git commit at submission: `e8c7543` (clean vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_39674609**

### Plain-language summary

**Purpose: a smoke test, not a validation run.** This is the first
end-to-end cluster execution since three changes landed this session,
none of which has run at cluster scale before: (1) a fix for a real
depth>=1 metric-routing bug (every Stage 1/Stage 2 neuron node was being
ranked with `correlation` instead of `f1`), (2) a full redesign of the
ranking-stage window (`MIN_PRED_EVENTS`/`MAX_WINDOW_ROWS`, replacing the
old fixed `CCM_WINDOW_ROWS=800` window for this purpose), and (3) the CCM
gate's own library-size sweep moved to absolute row counts
(`CCM_LIB_SIZES_ROWS`) instead of a percentage of that same window. See
`docs/review-findings.md`'s "Depth>=1 metric-routing bug" and "Window
sizing (MIN_PRED_EVENTS/MAX_WINDOW_ROWS) and CCM-gate absolute library
sizes" sections for the full narrative, real-data calibration, and test
evidence behind each.

**Compared against job_39674609 (2026-08-25) specifically because it's
the last job of this same pipeline** — the code diff below therefore
spans everything that changed since then (R12 through R22's own work,
plus the three items above), not something specific to this job alone;
most of those changes already have their own dedicated write-up in the
findings doc.

**Scale deliberately shrunk** for this smoke test, not a bigger run:
`REGION_CHANNEL_CAP` 30->3, `MDE_D` 10->2, `NESTED_M` 5->2. Resources cut
correspondingly (`--time` 4 days->2 hours, `--mem` 200G->16G,
`--cpus-per-task` 64->8) — see this job's own sbatch script comment block
for the specific reasoning (a real single-node timing measurement from
this session plus this pipeline's own history of underestimated Stage 1
cost at even modest scale). Submitted to a compute node deliberately, not
run locally: per-node ranking windows can now reach `MAX_WINDOW_ROWS`
(30000 rows), so this is compute-bound work regardless of how small
`REGION_CHANNEL_CAP`/`MDE_D` are — `docs/review-actions-v1.md`'s A4 was
amended this session to say so explicitly.
`TARGET_RANKING_WINDOW_ROWS`/`MIN_PRED_EVENTS`/`MAX_WINDOW_ROWS`/
`CCM_LIB_SIZES_ROWS` show as "unset" in job_39674609's own column below
only because that job predates these knobs existing at all, not because
anything was intentionally left at a different value.

**What to look for in this job's output**, per the report requested
alongside this smoke test: per-node resolved window lengths and target
pred-event counts, any nodes skipped for `MIN_PRED_EVENTS`
unreachability, the CCM gate's own new candidate-event-count diagnostic
alongside each fitted slope, selections per node distinguishing
budget-bound/event-starved/driverless zero-driver outcomes, and
wall-clock by stage (the still-open `REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=3->15` cost jump
this pipeline's own documentation flags is on the same surface this
smoke test exercises).

```diff
+def _resolve_target_ranking_window(target, full_df, usable_df, lib_ratio,
+                                    is_behavioral_target, target_ranking_window_rows,
+                                    min_pred_events, max_window_rows):
+    '''Window-sizing fix (found while verifying R22, docs/review-actions-v1.md
+    -- see docs/review-findings.md's own window-sizing section for the full
+    real-data investigation, including the two abandoned designs this
+    replaces): resolves the ranking-stage/E-auto-select window for one
+    node's own run_mde_for_target() call, decoupled from CCM_WINDOW_ROWS
+    (which stays governing the CCM gate's own convergence-curve library
+    sizing, now via absolute row counts -- see `ccm_lib_sizes_rows` in
+    run_mde_for_target()'s own docstring -- not this function's own frame
+    size at all).
+
+    BEHAVIORAL TARGETS (`is_behavioral_target=True`, always true at the
+    depth-0 seed): no TSLS reset-event concept applies (the target is a
+    genuine continuous trace, correlation-scored) -- window is simply
+    `min(target_ranking_window_rows, len(usable_df))`, a fixed constant
+    (default 1000), unrelated to firing rate. `min_pred_events` is not
+    used, `max_window_rows` is not used, and the returned event count is
+    always `None`.
+
+    NEURON TARGETS (`is_behavioral_target=False`, virtually every Stage 1/
+    Stage 2 node): grow the window W (in rows); within W, the PRED portion
+    is its own last `1 - lib_ratio` fraction of ROWS (the same split
+    `_ccm_window()` will later carve out of this exact W for the CCM
+    gate -- see that function). Count `target`'s real reset events that
+    fall in that row range -- never by events, only ever by rows -- and
+    stop at the smallest W where that count is >= `min_pred_events`.
+    `min_pred_events` is a plain, fixed integer (not a fraction of
+    anything neuron-specific): it answers "how many matched events does
+    f1 need before it is signal rather than noise", which is a property
+    of the metric, not of the neuron (see docs/review-findings.md for the
+    full reasoning behind abandoning the earlier
+    fraction-of-a-neuron's-own-total-events design, which made a busy
+    neuron face a stricter test than a quiet one for no stated reason, and
+    which -- checked against the WHOLE window rather than its pred
+    portion -- was later found on real data to pass while the pred
+    portion itself still had too few events to score anything on).
+
+    The search never grows W past `min(max_window_rows, len(usable_df))`
+    -- `max_window_rows` is a plain compute ceiling (not calibrated; see
+    load_config()'s own docstring), `len(usable_df)` is the leakage-safe
+    boundary this function's own caller has already trimmed to (see
+    run_mde_for_target()'s own LEAKAGE docstring). ALL event counting here
+    happens strictly within `usable_df` (i.e. `[0, B)`) -- never using
+    `full_df` rows at or past B, since sizing a search parameter from
+    held-out data is the same class of leakage the B boundary exists to
+    prevent (`full_df` is accepted only for signature symmetry with the
+    behavioral branch and is not read in this branch).
+
+    Returns (window_rows, pred_event_count). On success, `pred_event_count`
+    is the achieved count in the resolved window's own pred portion
+    (>= min_pred_events). On failure (`min_pred_events` unreachable
+    anywhere within the cap), returns (None, pred_event_count) where
+    pred_event_count is the best (largest) count achieved at ANY window
+    size tried, not necessarily at the cap itself -- the pred portion's
+    own event count is not guaranteed monotonic in W (both its edges only
+    ever move forward as W grows, but an event row can age out of the
+    portion's left edge in the same step before any new event row enters
+    at the right, so the count can dip locally) -- the caller can and
+    should report the shortfall as `min_pred_events - pred_event_count`
+    rather than silently scoring the node on too few events.'''
+    n_usable = len(usable_df)
+    if is_behavioral_target:
+        return min(target_ranking_window_rows, n_usable), None
+
+    cap = min(max_window_rows, n_usable)
+    if cap < 1:
+        return None, 0
+
+    usable_vals = usable_df[target].to_numpy()[:cap]
+    near_zero_threshold = tsls.infer_near_zero_threshold_from_true_tsls(
+        full_df[target].to_numpy())
+    # detect_reset_events_from_tsls classifies each row from only that row
+    # and the one before it (np.diff(..., prepend=x[0])), so truncating the
+    # input to `cap` rows first cannot change any detection within [0, cap).
+    event_indices = tsls.detect_reset_events_from_tsls(
+        usable_vals, near_zero_threshold=near_zero_threshold, drop_threshold=0.0)

+    # event_indices is sorted, so searchsorted gives the exact cumulative
+    # count up to any row bound with no explicit loop. pred_start[i] is the
+    # first row of the pred portion for window size w_candidates[i] -- the
+    # same `round(w * lib_ratio)` formula _ccm_window() uses for its own
+    # lib_end, so the final resolved window's pred portion here is exactly
+    # what the CCM gate will later carve out of it too.
+    w_candidates = np.arange(1, cap + 1)

+    hi = np.searchsorted(event_indices, w_candidates, side='left')

+    passing = pred_events_up_to_w >= min_pred_events

+        # see this function's own docstring for why the two can differ.
+        return None, int(pred_events_up_to_w.max())
+    first = int(np.argmax(passing))
+    return int(w_candidates[first]), int(pred_events_up_to_w[first])

+def partition_network(graph, targets, external_input_mode):
+    '''R14 (docs/review-actions-v1.md): partitions a MultiDiGraph built by
+    build_nested_mde_network() into interior nodes (>=1 discovered driver
+    -- genuinely simulated, their embedding built from those in-edges only,
+    see _embedding_spec_for()'s docstring) and external inputs (0 discovered
+    drivers -- what EXTERNAL_INPUT_MODE does with them is that function's
+    own concern, not this one's). Stored explicitly on the graph object
+    (`graph.graph['interior_nodes']`/`['external_inputs']`/
+    `['external_input_mode']`) rather than left implicit in edge counts, so
+    every consumer (embedding-spec construction, theta search, the 3D
+    figure, run-log reporting) reads the same authoritative classification
+    instead of re-deriving it.
+
+    A TARGET with zero discovered drivers is NEVER classified as an
+    external input, regardless of `external_input_mode` -- raises instead.
+    This is a failed network, not a valid one: feeding a target's own real
+    values back in as its "simulation" (EXTERNAL_INPUT_MODE='real_data')
+    and then scoring Generate() fidelity against those same real values
+    would be circular, producing a spuriously perfect score for exactly the
+    case that most needs to be flagged as a failure (confirmed against Run
+    A: head_position_y selected zero real drivers at depth 0 in that run --
+    this exemption exists because that is a real, not hypothetical, case).
+
+    Mutates `graph` in place; returns (interior_nodes, external_inputs) as
+    plain sets for convenience.'''
+    interior_nodes = set()
+    external_inputs = set()
+    for node in graph.nodes:
+        if graph.in_degree(node) == 0:
+            if node in targets:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"{node}: target selected zero drivers after nested-MDE (both stages) -- "
+                    f"this is a failed network, not a valid external input. A target can never "
+                    f"be exogenous: EXTERNAL_INPUT_MODE='real_data' would feed its own real "
+                    f"values back in as its \"simulation\" and then score fidelity against those "
+                    f"same real values, which is circular. Investigate why {node} found no "
+                    f"drivers (EMBED_DIM_RHO_MIN/CROSS_MAP_RHO_MIN/CCM_PREFILTER_RHO_MIN too "
+                    f"strict? too few candidate observables?) rather than working around it here."
+                )
+            external_inputs.add(node)
+        else:
+            interior_nodes.add(node)
+
+    graph.graph['interior_nodes'] = interior_nodes
+    graph.graph['external_inputs'] = external_inputs
+    graph.graph['external_input_mode'] = external_input_mode
+    return interior_nodes, external_inputs
+
+
+def _simulated_nodes(graph):
+    '''Nodes that actually go through gmn's own SMap/embedding machinery --
+    interior nodes always, plus external inputs too under
+    EXTERNAL_INPUT_MODE='self_simulate' (where they keep the old
+    unconditional self_delay_set embedding, see _embedding_spec_for()'s
+    docstring). Excludes real-data-mode external inputs: their Generate()/
+    Forecast() short-circuit to a real-data passthrough with no embedding
+    at all, so retuning theta for them (retune_theta_for_all_nodes(), which
+    calls _embedding_spec_for() directly) would either waste effort on an
+    inert result or crash on an empty spec.'''
+    external_inputs = graph.graph.get('external_inputs', set())
+    mode = graph.graph.get('external_input_mode', 'real_data')
+    if mode == 'self_simulate':
+        return list(graph.nodes)
+    return [n for n in graph.nodes if n not in external_inputs]
+
+
+def report_partition(graph, network_id, results_dir):
+    '''R14's own explicit reporting requirement: how many external inputs,
+    which observables and delays, and which interior nodes each feeds --
+    printed to the run log and written to a per-network CSV in
+    `results_dir` (partition_{network_id}.csv). Reads the classification
+    partition_network() already stored on `graph.graph` rather than
+    recomputing it.'''
+    external_inputs = graph.graph.get('external_inputs', set())
+    interior_nodes = graph.graph.get('interior_nodes', set())
+    mode = graph.graph.get('external_input_mode', 'real_data')
+
+    print(f'{network_id}: partition -- {len(interior_nodes)} interior node(s), '
+          f'{len(external_inputs)} external input(s) (EXTERNAL_INPUT_MODE={mode!r})', flush=True)
+
+    rows = []
+    for node in sorted(external_inputs):
+        out_edges = list(graph.out_edges(node, data=True))
+        if not out_edges:
+            print(f'  external input {node}: feeds nothing (dead-end leaf)', flush=True)
+            rows.append({'node': node, 'role': 'external_input', 'feeds': '', 'delay': ''})
+            continue
+        for _, fed_node, data in out_edges:
+            print(f'  external input {node} -> {fed_node} (delay {data["delay"]})', flush=True)
+            rows.append({'node': node, 'role': 'external_input', 'feeds': fed_node,
+                         'delay': data['delay']})
+    for node in sorted(interior_nodes):
+        rows.append({'node': node, 'role': 'interior', 'feeds': '', 'delay': ''})
+
+    partition_file = results_dir / f'partition_{network_id}.csv'
+    pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['node', 'role', 'feeds', 'delay']).to_csv(partition_file, index=False)
+

+def plot_3d_network(net_result, target_colors, save_path):
+    '''R14 (docs/review-actions-v1.md): the explicit 3D representation its
+    "leaf nodes become external inputs" decision requires -- MODE='MDE-GMN'
+    only (needs the per-edge delay data and interior/external partition
+    only that mode's MultiDiGraph has, both absent from MODE='GMN''s plain
+    DiGraph). x-y plane: a standard graph layout of the real-observable
+    (delay=0) backbone from Stages 1 and 2 -- the same structural skeleton
+    draw_colored_network() draws in 2D. z axis: for every node, one vertical
+    stick per delay!=0 driver nested-MDE discovered for it, rising from
+    z=0 to z=|delay| at that node's own (x, y) -- literally "the delayed
+    observables that further drive each node," stacked above it rather than
+    laid out in the plane, since a lagged driver is a copy of an existing
+    real observable at a different point in time, not a new spatial
+    position. External inputs (partition_network()'s own classification,
+    read from graph.graph -- not re-derived here) are drawn as a distinct
+    marker shape (triangle vs. circle) from interior nodes, per the task's
+    own explicit requirement, independent of target coloring.'''
+    from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D  # noqa: F401 -- registers the 3d projection
+
+    graph = net_result['network']['Graph']
+    interior_nodes = graph.graph.get('interior_nodes', set())
+    external_inputs = graph.graph.get('external_inputs', set())
+
+    real_edges = [(u, v) for u, v, d in graph.edges(data=True) if d['delay'] == 0]
+    backbone = nx.DiGraph()
+    backbone.add_nodes_from(graph.nodes)
+    backbone.add_edges_from(real_edges)
+    pos = nx.spring_layout(backbone, seed=0)
+
+    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
+    ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')
+
+    for u, v in real_edges:
+        xu, yu = pos[u]
+        xv, yv = pos[v]
+        ax.plot([xu, xv], [yu, yv], [0, 0], color='gray', linewidth=1, alpha=0.6, zorder=1)
+
+    for u, v, data in graph.edges(data=True):
+        if data['delay'] == 0:
+            continue
+        x, y = pos[v]
+        z = abs(data['delay'])
+        ax.plot([x, x], [y, y], [0, z], color='steelblue', linewidth=1, alpha=0.5, zorder=2)
+        ax.scatter([x], [y], [z], color='steelblue', marker='s', s=15, zorder=6)
+        ax.text(x, y, z, u, fontsize=5, color='steelblue')
+
+    for node in graph.nodes:
+        x, y = pos[node]
+        is_external = node in external_inputs
+        color = target_colors.get(node, 'tab:orange' if is_external else 'tab:blue')
+        marker = '^' if is_external else 'o'
+        ax.scatter([x], [y], [0], color=color, marker=marker, s=100,
+                   edgecolors='black', linewidths=0.8, zorder=5)
+        ax.text(x, y, 0, node, fontsize=7, fontweight='bold')
+
+    node_handles = [
+        plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markersize=10,
+                   markerfacecolor='tab:blue', markeredgecolor='black', label='interior'),
+        plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='^', color='w', markersize=10,
+                   markerfacecolor='tab:orange', markeredgecolor='black', label='external input'),
+    ]
+    ax.legend(handles=node_handles, loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 1.0),
+              title=f"n_interior={len(interior_nodes)}, n_external={len(external_inputs)}")
+    ax.set_xlabel('X (real-observable network layout)')
+    ax.set_ylabel('Y (real-observable network layout)')
+    ax.set_zlabel('|delay| (lagged driver depth)')
+    ax.set_title(f"3D network projection ({net_result['network_id']})")
+    fig.savefig(save_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
+    plt.close(fig)
+
```

that did run the full 4 days, one (job_39069787, code predating the
inner-pool parallelism/CCM-pre-filter/Stage2-recursion fixes) peaked at
~114GB against its 128G request -- a genuinely close call, close enough
that it's worth real headroom rather than assuming the newer code's much
lower measured usage (job_39083467, ~11.4GB; job_39671271 itself,
~6.1GB about an hour in as of this submission) is guaranteed to hold for
the entire run. 200G stays well under this partition's 500G/node cap
while giving ~1.75x the room job_39069787's own peak needed.

`--mem` was bumped, this job submitted, then reverted back to 128G
immediately afterward in the working tree -- Slurm snapshots a script's
full contents at submission time (same round-trip pattern used for
job_37946959), so this doesn't affect what job_39674609 actually
requested; it just keeps the standing sbatch file's default unchanged
until there's a confirmed reason (an actual OOM, not just a historical
close call from now-superseded code) to raise it permanently.

## Job 39671000

Generated: 2026-08-25T13:20:48+09:00

Git commit at submission: `e33810e` (uncommitted local changes vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_39656077**

### Plain-language summary

Same medium-scale config as job_39656077 (unchanged: REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=30,
MDE_D=10, NESTED_M=5, TP=10, GENERATE_LENGTH=40, CCM_PREFILTER_RHO_MIN=0.2,
CCM_PREFILTER_E=7, STAGE2_ALLOW_REAL_OBSERVABLES=false) -- this
resubmission exists purely to cluster-validate the same significant
Python restructuring described below, not to test a new parameter
combination. job_39656077 itself is still RUNNING as of this submission
(started ~2h ago, on the pre-restructuring code) and is left alone; this
is a separate, independent job on the current code.

**What changed in the code** (see diff below for the full change; two
fixes, made together per explicit request, after review found the
previous CCM-pre-filter integration didn't match the intended algorithm):

1. **Stage 2 now recurses.** Previously, Stage 1 (real-observable-only
   nested-MDE) ran to completion, then Stage 2 (lagged-embedding
   attachment, or lagged+real when STAGE2_ALLOW_REAL_OBSERVABLES=true) ran
   once over the final node set -- even a Stage-2-selected *real*
   observable driver was always a dead-end leaf, never itself searched
   for its own further drivers. `attach_lag_embeddings()` (the old
   separate Stage 2 function) is now folded into `build_nested_mde_network()`
   as a per-wave pass: every BFS wave runs both a Stage 1 pass and a
   Stage 2 pass, and *either* stage's real-observable (delay=0) picks
   feed the next wave. Verified on real data locally before this
   submission (isolated Stage-2-style probe calls' real-observable picks
   were confirmed to actually recurse into their own further nested-MDE
   round, on both this pipeline's 40Hz data and simple-mde-gmn.py's 1Hz
   data) -- see the nested-MDE-stage2-recursion memory for the full
   writeup. This job runs with STAGE2_ALLOW_REAL_OBSERVABLES=false
   (unchanged default), so it does not exercise this specific behavior
   change -- it mainly validates fix 2 below and general no-crash/
   no-performance-regression at cluster scale, since fix 1 was already
   confirmed correct locally.
2. **CCM pre-filter now runs before depth-0, not after.** Previously each
   target's first-round ("depth-0") driver search ran in `main()` against
   the *full*, unfiltered observable pool, and the CCM pre-filter only
   narrowed the pool afterward, inside `build_network()` -- this was the
   root cause of the `CA1_12_tsls`/`CA1_22` crash job_39655803/39655804
   fixed with a fallback in `observable_and_delay()`. That fallback is
   now closer to a pure safety net (still needed for cross-job cache
   reuse of an older result) rather than the normal path: `main()` now
   runs the pre-filter once per target group *before* seeding depth-0, so
   depth-0 and every later nested-MDE round search the exact same
   filtered pool.

### Parameter changes (tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch)

_No parameter changes._

### Batch script design changes (tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch, excludes parameter block above)

_No changes._

Generated: 2026-08-25T13:20:44+09:00

Git commit at submission: `e33810e` (uncommitted local changes vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_39655803**

### Plain-language summary

Same medium-scale config as job_39655803 (unchanged: REGION_CHANNEL_CAP=30,
MDE_D=10, NESTED_M=5, TP=10, GENERATE_LENGTH=40, CCM_PREFILTER_RHO_MIN=0.2,
CCM_PREFILTER_E=3, STAGE2_ALLOW_REAL_OBSERVABLES=false) -- this
resubmission exists purely to cluster-validate the same significant
Python restructuring described below, not to test a new parameter
combination. job_39655803 itself is still RUNNING as of this submission
(started ~2h ago, on the pre-restructuring code) and is left alone; this
is a separate, independent job on the current code.

**What changed in the code** (mirrors job_39671000's own tsls-mde-gmn.py
entry -- two fixes, made together per explicit request, after review
found the previous CCM-pre-filter integration didn't match the intended
algorithm):

1. **Stage 2 now recurses.** Previously, Stage 1 (real-observable-only
   nested-MDE) ran to completion, then Stage 2 (lagged-embedding
   attachment, or lagged+real when STAGE2_ALLOW_REAL_OBSERVABLES=true) ran
   once over the final node set -- even a Stage-2-selected *real*
   observable driver was always a dead-end leaf, never itself searched
   for its own further drivers. `attach_lag_embeddings()` (the old
   separate Stage 2 function) is now folded into `build_nested_mde_network()`
   as a per-wave pass: every BFS wave runs both a Stage 1 pass and a
   Stage 2 pass, and *either* stage's real-observable (delay=0) picks
   feed the next wave. Verified on real data locally before this
   submission (isolated Stage-2-style probe calls' real-observable picks
   were confirmed to actually recurse into their own further nested-MDE
   round) -- see the nested-MDE-stage2-recursion memory for the full
   writeup. This job runs with STAGE2_ALLOW_REAL_OBSERVABLES=false
   (unchanged default), so it does not exercise this specific behavior
   change -- it mainly validates fix 2 below and general no-crash/
   no-performance-regression at cluster scale, since fix 1 was already
   confirmed correct locally.
2. **CCM pre-filter now runs before depth-0, not after.** Previously each
   target's first-round ("depth-0") driver search ran in `main()` against
   the *full*, unfiltered observable pool, and the CCM pre-filter only
   narrowed the pool afterward, inside `build_network()` -- this was the
   root cause of the `CA1_22` crash job_39655803 itself fixed with a
   fallback in `observable_and_delay()`. That fallback is now closer to a
   pure safety net (still needed for cross-job cache reuse of an older
   result) rather than the normal path: `main()` now runs the pre-filter
   once per target group *before* seeding depth-0, so depth-0 and every
   later nested-MDE round search the exact same filtered pool.

### Parameter changes (simple-mde-gmn.sbatch)

_No parameter changes._

### Batch script design changes (simple-mde-gmn.sbatch, excludes parameter block above)

_No changes._

## Job 39655804

Generated: 2026-08-25T11:10:12+09:00

Git commit at submission: `e33810e` (uncommitted local changes vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_39605473**

### Plain-language summary

Resubmission of job_39605473 (same medium-scale config, unchanged) after
it crashed 3m35s in with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base
10: 'CA1_12_tsls'` inside `observable_and_delay()`. Root cause: the CCM
pre-filter shrinks the `raw_columns` a given `build_nested_mde_network()`
call sees, but a depth-0 target's `mde_results` entry was computed once
in `main()` against the *full*, unfiltered pool, before the pre-filter
ever ran -- so a depth-0-selected real observable can legitimately be
absent from Stage 1's own (filtered) `raw_columns`, and the old
membership-only classification (`if column_name in raw_columns: ... else:
parse as delay-suffixed`) crashed trying to parse it as one instead of
recognizing it as its own real, delay=0 name. Fixed by adding a
marker-presence fallback to `observable_and_delay()` (only reached when
membership fails): a real channel name never contains the literal
`DELAY_MARKER` (`'::delay'`) substring, so this is a safe, general
classification rule, not a special case for the pre-filter specifically.
Verified directly (unit-level, both files) against the exact crash
scenario plus two regression checks (delay-suffixed names still parse;
membership still wins when available) before this resubmission. Same
fix applied identically to simple-mde-gmn.py (job_39655803's own entry).

### Parameter changes (tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch)

_No parameter changes._

### Batch script design changes (tsls-mde-gmn.sbatch, excludes parameter block above)

_No changes._

### Python pipeline changes (tsls-mde-gmn.py)

```diff
--- job_39605473/tsls-mde-gmn.py
+++ job_39655804/tsls-mde-gmn.py
@@ -1080,10 +1080,31 @@
     underlying (observable, delay) pair. Delay=0 candidates are just the
     raw observable name itself (see expand_delay_columns()'s docstring for
     why that delay isn't also given a suffixed alias) -- checked against
-    `raw_columns` rather than by string shape alone, in case a real channel
-    name were ever to collide with the delay-suffix marker.'''
+    `raw_columns` FIRST rather than by string shape alone, in case a real
+    channel name were ever to collide with the delay-suffix marker
+    (membership is the authoritative signal whenever available).
+
+    Falls back to a marker-presence check (bug found 2026-08-25, job
+    39605472/39605473 -- ported from simple-mde-gmn.py's own identical
+    fix) when `column_name` isn't in `raw_columns` at all:
+    ccm_prefilter_observables() can shrink the `raw_columns` a given
+    build_nested_mde_network()/attach_lag_embeddings() call sees, but a
+    depth-0 node's mde_results entry was computed once in main(), against
+    the *full*, unfiltered candidate pool, before that filtering ever ran
+    -- so a depth-0-selected real observable can legitimately be absent
+    from this call's own (filtered) `raw_columns` while still being a
+    perfectly valid delay=0 column. Without this fallback,
+    _parse_delayed_column_name() crashes on any such name (confirmed:
+    `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'CA1_12_tsls'`)
+    since it has no delay marker to parse. Residual risk is unchanged from
+    before this fallback existed: only a real channel name that is BOTH
+    missing from `raw_columns` AND happens to contain the literal
+    `DELAY_MARKER` substring would still be misclassified -- this
+    codebase's actual naming scheme never produces that.'''
     if column_name in raw_columns:
         return column_name, 0
+    if DELAY_MARKER not in column_name:
+        return column_name, 0
     return _parse_delayed_column_name(column_name)
 
 
```

```diff
+    39605472/39605473) when `column_name` isn't in `raw_columns` at all:
+    ccm_prefilter_observables() can shrink the `raw_columns` a given
+    build_nested_mde_network()/attach_lag_embeddings() call sees, but a
+    depth-0 node's mde_results entry was computed once in main(), against
+    the *full*, unfiltered candidate pool, before that filtering ever ran
+    -- so a depth-0-selected real observable can legitimately be absent
+    from this call's own (filtered) `raw_columns` while still being a
+    perfectly valid delay=0 column. Without this fallback,
+    _parse_delayed_column_name() crashes on any such name (confirmed:
+    `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'CA1_22'`) since
+    it has no delay marker to parse. Residual risk is unchanged from
+    before this fallback existed: only a real channel name that is BOTH
+    missing from `raw_columns` AND happens to contain the literal
+    `DELAY_MARKER` substring would still be misclassified -- this
+    codebase's actual naming scheme (CA1_N/mPFC_N/OFC_N/head_position_*)
+    never produces that.'''
     if column_name in raw_columns:
         return column_name, 0
+    if DELAY_MARKER not in column_name:
+        return column_name, 0
     return _parse_delayed_column_name(column_name)
 
 
```

## Job 39417809

Not a pipeline job -- no JOB_LOG entry was ever auto-generated for it
(it wasn't submitted via `scripts/batch/submit.sh`), so this entry is
reconstructed after the fact from `sacct` at the user's request, rather
than following the usual parameter-diff format above/below.

`sacct`: `JobName=bash`, `Partition=compute`, `NodeList=deigo010901`,
`ReqMem=1G`, `Submit=2026-08-23T13:44:06`, `Elapsed=00:01:24`,
`State=TIMEOUT`. This is one of a long, automated series of ad-hoc
`srun --nodelist=<node> ... bash -c "..."` diagnostic probes (`sacct`
shows ~15 more, every ~10 minutes, alternating across
`deigo010901`/`010904`/`010905`/`010911`, spanning at least
2026-08-23T13:03 through 17:21+) checking whether `/bucket` had
recovered from a read-only outage on specific compute nodes -- this is
the "2026-08-23 outage" job_39656077's own entry later refers back to.

### Outcome

**TIMEOUT**, and notably *not* a fast failure like its 15+ sibling
probes (which all `FAILED` in 0-56 seconds, consistent with `/bucket`
returning a fast `Read-only file system` error). This one instead hung
for its own full ~1m24s time limit before being killed -- suggesting
`/bucket` was genuinely unresponsive on `deigo010901` at that specific
moment (13:44), not just cleanly read-only, a distinct and slightly more
severe symptom than the surrounding probes. No `.out`/`.err` file
survives to confirm the exact command run (ad-hoc `srun`, not archived
by this project's usual pipeline output-preservation convention).

## Job 39354205

Generated: 2026-08-23T01:40:58+09:00

Git commit at submission: `e33810e` (uncommitted local changes vs. HEAD)

Compared against: **job_39183767**

### Plain-language summary

First of 6 resubmissions recovering the production-scale `Tp` sweep
(job_38871293, job_38883548/49/51/56 -- this job resumes job_38871293,
`TP=30`) plus the separate validation-scale smoke test job_39025340
(resumed by job_39354345), all of which failed. Diffed here against
job_39183767 (a newer, unrelated smoke-test-scale job at 20/5/4) purely
because that's the immediately-preceding simple-mde-gmn.sbatch
submission -- every actual parameter below was restored to
job_38871293's own original value, reconstructed from JOB_LOG.md's full
diff chain (traced parameter-by-parameter all the way back to
job_36515744/job_37939058, cross-checked two independent ways), not
inherited from job_39183767's own smoke-test config.

**Diagnosis, corrected from the initial "OOM" report:** `sacct`'s
`.batch`-step-level data confirms all 6 original jobs were genuinely
OOM-killed (MaxRSS ~311-313GB against `--mem=300G` on every one of
them, including job_39025340 at a 33x-smaller `REGION_CHANNEL_CAP` --
memory usage tracked wall-clock exposure, not problem size, which is the
first clue something other than "the computation needs N GB" was going
on). 5 of the 6 additionally show job-level `TIMEOUT` rather than `OOM`
-- `slurmstepd`'s own log line resolves this: `Detected 1 oom_kill event
in StepId=38871293.batch` fired mid-run, then the job kept running
(minus whatever got killed) until the separate 4-day wall clock also
expired, so both labels are true of the same underlying event, just
timestamped differently by Slurm's own accounting.

**Root cause, found by inspecting the actual `.err` files still on
`/flash`:** each is 68-71GB (23GB for job_39025340), essentially all one
repeated pyEDM `UserWarning` -- `Simplex: FindNeighbors() : Failed to
find knn outside exclusionRadius X for some predictions. Consider
reducing knn Y.` -- fired by `pyEDM/Neighbors.py` every time a
prediction has fewer valid neighbors than requested outside the current
exclusionRadius (purely informational; the prediction still runs).
`EXCLUSION_RADIUS=auto` deliberately varies exclusionRadius per call, so
X/Y differ every time, which means the interpolated message text is
"new" to Python's default per-message warning dedup on every single
occurrence -- nothing in this pipeline had ever added a `warnings`
filter, so literally every occurrence got printed and flushed. That
volume of buffered/flushed stdio across a multi-day run is a plausible,
well-evidenced driver of both the OOM-killed subprocess and the
eventual timeout; it isn't a hypothetical -- the same class of pyEDM-
warning-spam problem was already flagged once before (JOB_LOG.md's
job_38870714 entry, `.err` at ~23MB for a tiny smoke test) but never
actually fixed at the source, only relocated (/home -> /flash) as the
volume kept growing.

**Fix applied** (per user direction, before any of these 6
resubmissions): `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sitecustomize.py`
(the same venv-wide, auto-imported-at-interpreter-startup file already
used for the earlier pyEDM Pool-spawn fix -- see that section of this
same file) now also registers
`warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=UserWarning,
message=r'.*FindNeighbors\(\)\s*:')`. Verified directly against the
exact message-construction code in `pyEDM/Neighbors.py` (both warning
variants share the `<name>: FindNeighbors() :` prefix) and against a
synthetic `warnings.warn()` call reproducing the real message text --
confirmed suppressed, with an unrelated warning left untouched as a
